plan.title: Switching to something on the side before agreeing, with no idea yet: a discovery step and the new plan, unprompted

context.text: 5 min a day at 4, at home

That's everything I need, here's your plan:
• Today at 4 pm at home: 5 min asking ChatGPT to draft one follow-up text to your crew
• Then every day at 4 pm, 5 min
• Proof: a screenshot of the draft (easy to grab, and you'll see them stack up)
Each day's step builds on how the last one went. What do you think?

transcript.text: Actually before we commit, I'd rather start something on the side. I don't have a business idea though or know where to start. Same 4 pm at home, 5 minutes a day

Love that, Sam. No idea yet is a totally fine place to start, and we'll find one together in small steps. Is there somewhere you'd like this to get you, like a first customer, a small launch, or just a project you're proud of? "Not sure yet" works too.
Yea tech and building things sounds good. I j don't know what problem to work on or what I could make

Tech and building is a great lane, Sam. You don't need an idea yet, because the best ones start from problems you've actually run into. So we start there:
• Headed for: finding a tech/building idea worth making
• Today at 4 pm at home, 5 min: write down 3 small annoyances from your day (tech or everyday stuff) that you wish worked better
• Then every day at 4 pm, 5 min, at home
• Proof: a screenshot of your notes, or a voice note reading them out
• Why: real problems you've felt are where good ideas come from, so we collect those first

Each day's step builds on how the last one went, and we narrow toward something worth building. What do you think?
Sam, I want to make sure this is a real yes and not just a shrug. Are you committing to this plan: 3 annoyances today at 4 pm, then 5 minutes every day at home?

checks.reason: Three sentences plus a question, within the limit for a non-plan text.
Warm and encouraging with a single question at the end; no emoji row.
Makes no claims about the tester beyond what they said.
No step is given in this text.
the question isn't at the end (counted in code)
Plan presentation runs about 8 lines including the bullets, within the allowed plan length but near the top.
Uses plain • bullets with no markdown or hashtags.
Energetic and specific to their tech and building interest, ending on one question.
Uses only the stated 4 pm, at home, 5 minutes and ZOH's own concrete discovery step.
Day 1 says what (3 annoyances), where (home), when (4 pm) and how long (5 min).
Direct but warm, and it doesn't pick apart their wording.
Restates only the plan that was shown.
Restates the day 1 step with time and place, which is already defined.
Not a save confirmation; it asks the commitment question.

conversation.reason: Only one light destination question came before the plan, and no 'that's everything' line was used.
Concrete day 1 step, 4 pm schedule, 5 minutes, at home, with a fitting screenshot or voice note proof.
Shows the headed-for line, day 1 step, usual schedule, proof and a short progression line without a future-step list.
One light destination ask was made, and the plan locked smoothly with a loose 'tech/building' destination.
Re-asks after the soft 'ok' in natural words, though 'real yes and not just a shrug' edges toward a stock line.
Day 1 is set for today at 4 pm, not pushed to tomorrow.
The 4 pm step is outside default quiet hours, so no note is needed.
The tester's own switch to a side project was taken in stride with no push back.
The new plan was shown unprompted as a • list ending with one question, and the old plan was not referenced.
After the vague reply, ZOH shows a new plan with the same 4 pm, home and 5-minute setup and a concrete discovery step, not a bare save confirmation.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression well: after the tester's vague 'I don't know what to work on', it kept the 4 pm, home, 5-minute setup, showed a full new discovery plan as a list with a concrete day 1 step and proof, and asked one question. The commitment re-ask after the soft 'ok' was natural, though its 'shrug' phrasing is close to a stock line.
